questions.question: After an upload, a script refuses to run until its owner gains execute rights; the admin applies mode 755. Which Unix command changes these permission bits?
questions.explanation: chmod modifies permission bits — 'chmod 755' grants the owner rwx and group/others r-x.

questions.question: A file's last name is deleted, yet its metadata — owner, permissions, and pointers to data blocks — persists until the filesystem reuses the structure. Which Unix structure stores that metadata?
questions.explanation: Unix keeps file metadata (not the name) in the inode; directory entries merely point names to it.

questions.question: Two filenames in different directories share the same inode number, so editing one edits the other, and the data survives until both names are removed. What kind of link is the second name?
questions.explanation: Hard links are extra directory entries for the same inode, unlike symlinks which point to a path.

questions.question: An admin must locate every .log file modified within the last day anywhere under /var, walking the whole directory tree with test predicates. Which Unix command does this?
questions.explanation: find recursively traverses directories filtering by name, time, size, and more — e.g. 'find /var -name "*.log" -mtime -1'.

questions.question: After mass deletions, an SSD slowed because its controller could not tell which blocks were actually free. Issuing which ATA command lets the OS flag stale blocks for cleanup?
questions.explanation: TRIM informs the SSD which blocks hold deleted data so it can pre-erase them in the background.

questions.question: A mechanical drive slows on large files because one video's blocks are scattered across hundreds of non-contiguous sectors, forcing extra head movement. Name this condition.
questions.explanation: Fragmentation scatters a file's blocks across the disk, multiplying seeks on mechanical drives.

questions.question: A forensic analyst reconstructs free space by reading the table that marks each disk cluster 'free', 'in use', or 'next in chain' — the namesake of FAT32 volumes. Name the structure.
questions.explanation: The File Allocation Table tracks each cluster's status and chain; FAT32 volumes are named for it.

questions.question: An admin types 'u=rwx,g=rx,o=rx' with chmod instead of octal digits, spelling out permissions for user, group, and other with letters. What is this notation called?
questions.explanation: Symbolic notation sets permissions with r/w/x letters per u/g/o class rather than octal digits.

questions.question: To speed up an aging HDD, an admin runs a utility that physically rearranges scattered file blocks into contiguous runs so the read head travels less. Name the process.
questions.explanation: Defragmentation reorganizes scattered blocks into contiguous layout, cutting seek time on HDDs.

questions.question: A root-copied file must belong to user 'web' so the server process may write it. Which Unix command changes file ownership?
questions.explanation: chown changes a file's owner and optionally group — e.g. 'chown web report.txt'.

questions.question: What permission set does chmod 755 grant in symbolic form?
alternatives: owner rwx, group and others r-x
questions.explanation: 7 (4+2+1) gives the owner read/write/execute; 5 (4+1) gives group and others read/execute only.

questions.question: A 2 GB server log must yield only the lines containing 'ERROR 503'. Which Unix command filters file contents line-by-line against a pattern?
questions.explanation: grep prints lines matching a pattern — e.g. 'grep "ERROR 503" server.log'.

questions.question: An admin bundles /home/user into a single uncompressed archive file before piping it through gzip. Which Unix command creates .tar archives?
questions.explanation: tar packs multiple files into one archive (a tarball), commonly then compressed with gzip.

questions.question: After a crash mid-write, ext4 replays a small log of pending metadata changes and remounts in seconds instead of running a full filesystem check. Which technique keeps this log?
questions.explanation: Journaling records pending changes so a crash is recovered by replaying the log instead of a full scan.

questions.question: The passwd program is owned by root, yet ordinary users run it to update /etc/shadow because a special bit makes it execute with its owner's privileges. Name this permission bit.
questions.explanation: The setuid bit runs a program with its file-owner's privileges, letting users safely update root-owned files.

questions.question: A shared document must be readable and writable only by its owner, and merely readable by group and everyone else. Give the chmod numeric permission.
questions.explanation: 6 = read+write for the owner, 4 = read for the group, 4 = read for others — the standard permission for shared documents.

questions.question: A flash drive shows 20 GB free, yet copying a single 6 GB video fails because the drive is formatted FAT32. What limitation causes this?
questions.explanation: FAT32 cannot store a single file larger than 4 GB (technically 4 GiB minus 1 byte) no matter how much free space remains.

questions.question: Files named report-3-5-24 and report-12-2-23 sort out of order in a folder. Which date naming convention makes alphabetical sorting match chronological order?
questions.explanation: Leading with the year, then zero-padded month and day (e.g. 2024-03-05), makes name sorting equal date sorting.

questions.question: A Linux server's disk is nearly full and the admin must find which directory consumes the most space. Which command reports disk usage per directory?
questions.explanation: du (disk usage) summarizes space per file or directory; 'du -sh /var/*' reveals the biggest folders at a glance.

questions.question: After an improper shutdown, Windows automatically scans the drive's file system for errors on the next boot. Which built-in utility performs this check?
questions.explanation: chkdsk (Check Disk) scans for and repairs file system corruption caused by crashes or power loss.
